note: Issue 4722, silent face. repro.hlsl asks for row-major layout via #pragma pack_matrix(row_major) on a template-dependent matrix<T,X,Y>. The symptom is that the request is dropped and the DEFAULT orientation is emitted instead, with no diagnostic and exit 0 -- so there is no error text and no exit code to test, and the predicate has to read the emitted DXIL. Clause 1 reads the orientation out of the cbuffer layout block of the disassembly (the same information is in the field annotation metadata, DxilMDHelper tag 2 = {rows, cols, orientation}, MatrixOrientation::ColumnMajor == 2). Clause 2 is the anti-vacuity anchor: !dx.entryPoints only exists if codegen completed, so a release that rejected the input cannot satisfy this predicate. This is a PRESENCE predicate by design -- an absence formulation ("no row_major") would be satisfied for free by any release that failed to compile at all. CONTROLS: control-nontemplate-row-major.hlsl is the same declaration without the template and must NOT match; control-nontemplate-default.hlsl must match, which is what measures the default orientation on the build under test instead of assuming it; control-nontemplate-column-major.hlsl must match, proving the predicate reads genuine column-major layout; control-template-column-major.hlsl must match AND produce byte-identical DXIL to repro.hlsl, which is the decisive evidence (see manual-case-identity.txt); control-template-default.hlsl compiled with -Zpr must NOT match, proving the command-line flag does reach the template path and so the defect is the source-level request, not templates plus orientation generally.
